content.thinking:
I should note that the "flag was toggled" conclusion is really an inference from evaluation counts flipping at 17:53, not something confirmed by the flag provider's audit history, which actually shows zero recent changes—that's an important assumption to flag. Also worth noting: no mitigation was actually attempted, the incident was escalated with only an unverified draft PR #45, and since the service hadn't recovered by the last metrics read, the duration I'm calculating is really just a lower bound.

I'm also wary about the impact numbers—the instructions seem to warn against restating given figures as if I'd computed them myself, so I should describe the impact qualitatively rather than citing specific error-rate percentages, sticking to something like "a substantial minority of account-page requests failed" without numbers, aside from timestamps.

The root cause traces to a divide-by-zero when computing a shopper's monthly spend, triggered when a feature flag flipped from off to fully on within about a minute (17:53–17:54), causing every render on that path to error; there's no deploy or config change in that window, so the flip is inferred from evaluation logs rather than a recorded flag-history entry. I'm keeping the executive summary free of specific file or component names, describing things plainly as "the shop's account page" and "a newly enabled feature."

For duration, the outage started at 17:53 and was still ongoing at the last metrics read around 17:58 (a lower bound), with an alert firing at 17:58, an automated responder investigating but unable to act, and escalation with a draft fix proposed at 18:00 — no confirmed resolution yet.

assumptions: The feature flag flip is an inference, not a confirmed event: the flag provider's history was queried and returned no recent flag changes. The only evidence of a flip is the shift in per-minute flag-evaluation counts written by the service itself.
Who or what turned the flag on, and whether it was a deliberate rollout, is unknown. No deploy or release was recorded in windows extending back over a week before onset.

The causal link between the flag's on-path and the ZeroDivisionError is drawn from correlation in the logs (errors appear in the same minute evaluations first show 'on'); the code at spend_summary.py:47 was not independently inspected or reproduced during the incident.

The divide-by-zero condition presumably depends on shopper data (e.g. a zero denominator such as no billing days or no orders in the period), but nothing in the evidence identifies which shoppers or what input triggers it.
No mitigation was attempted and nothing was rolled back, so nothing confirms that disabling the flag would stop the errors — that remains the expected but untested remedy.
The draft pull request (PR #45) is a proposed fix only. It was not reviewed, merged or deployed within the incident, and its correctness is unverified.
The end of impact is unknown. The service was still failing at the last minute of metrics read, so every duration and impact figure in the incident record is a lower bound.
Baseline errors before onset were client disconnects, which were assumed to be normal background noise unrelated to this fault.
input.executive_summary: Starting at 17:53 UTC on 26 September 2026, a large share of shoppers loading their account page got an error instead. The cause was a newly switched-on account feature whose code crashes while calculating a shopper's monthly spending total; before the switch, the same pages were rendering normally aside from ordinary background noise. Monitoring raised an alert at 17:58 and the automated responder investigated immediately, but it produced no safe corrective action it could take on its own, so it opened a draft code change for a human engineer at 18:00 and escalated. At the point the incident record ends, the service had not recovered and nothing had actually been changed in production, so the outage was still ongoing and its true length and cost are at least as large as what was recorded, not exactly that. Other parts of the shop were not implicated; the failures were confined to account-page requests.
input.root_cause: When the `monthly-spend-feature` flag began evaluating "on" at 17:53 (partial at 17:53, fully on from 17:54), the enabled code path in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47` divided by zero while computing a shopper's monthly spend, so every account-page render that took that path failed with ZeroDivisionError. No deploy, release or other production change was recorded on the service in any window searched, and the flag provider reported no recent flag change either — the flip is inferred from the per-minute flag-evaluation counts in the service's own logs, which go from all-off before 17:53 to all-on after, exactly tracking the arrival of the ZeroDivisionError lines.
